clue.text: Litter: a good way to make something of it?

parts.note: a good way off means a long distance, so far
to make something of it is to pick a quarrel, a row

explanation.surface: A question about the best method of exploiting rubbish lying around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Litter' looks like rubbish but is the definition: a sow's brood of piglets.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrow is the set of piglets a sow bears at one birth, a litter.

clue.text: Heading for farm, more unusual cattle feed

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

parts.note: odder means stranger, more unusual

explanation.surface: Someone sets off for a farm where the cattle feed is rather peculiar.
explanation.definitionFit: Fodder is dried food such as hay given to livestock.

clue.text: Rice dish is too much in centre of Verona

indicators.note: in places the earlier pieces inside the central letters of the city
the centre of the six-letter city is its middle two letters

parts.note: OTT is short for over the top, too much

explanation.surface: A rice dish served in central Verona is excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian rice dish cooked slowly in stock.

clue.text: Short one, tune being broadcast

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: an air is a tune or melody

explanation.surface: A brief tune being played on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: On air is the broadcasting phrase for a programme going out live.

clue.text: Penny increase gets approval

parts.note: a raise is an increase, as in pay

explanation.surface: A small pay rise earns someone's approval.
explanation.definitionFit: Praise is expressed approval or commendation of someone.

clue.text: Playwright ran hostel in resort

indicators.note: read as re-sort, so the letters are sorted again into a new order

explanation.surface: A dramatist who ran a hostel at a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a seaside town but reads as re-sort. Jack Rosenthal was an English TV dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Rosenthal was a British dramatist, writer of The Evacuees and Barmitzvah Boy.

clue.text: First sign

definitions.meaning: coming at the beginning, the opening one
to mark a document with one's ...

explanation.definitionFit: Initial means first in order, and to initial a document is to sign it with one's initials.

clue.text: Come out of European Union? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means the word is incomplete, missing its last letter

parts.note: a merger is a union of two bodies

explanation.surface: A question about leaving the EU, but only partly.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points at Brexit; 'Come out' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To emerge is to come out into view from somewhere hidden.

clue.text: Burial site in field church overlooked

indicators.note: overlooked means left out, so the church letters are dropped from the field

parts.note: a pitch is a playing field

explanation.surface: A grave in a field that the nearby church ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit is a hole in the ground, used as a mass grave or burial place.

clue.text: Therefore in error if pawn moved and captured man?

indicators.note: in puts the therefore word inside the rearranged letters
moved, as a chess piece is moved, means these letters are shifted about

parts.note: so means therefore

explanation.surface: A chess player blunders by moving a pawn, and a man is taken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Captured man' in chess means a taken piece; here it is a soldier taken by the enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner of war is a combatant taken and held captive by the enemy.

clue.text: Proscribed, as opposed to prescribed thinking? They'll monitor that

definitions.text: Proscribed, as opposed to prescribed thinking? They'll monitor that

parts.words: Proscribed, as opposed to prescribed thinking? They'll monitor that
parts.note: in Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four a force watches for forbidden ideas, as opposed to the approved ones

explanation.surface: A puzzle about who polices banned rather than approved ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: In George Orwell's novel Nineteen Eighty-Four, 'thoughtcrime' is detected by a secret police force.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwell's secret force punishes forbidden ideas, so it monitors proscribed thinking.

clue.text: Hopelessness of French husband and wife

parts.note: des is French for 'of the' (plural)
a married couple are a pair

explanation.surface: A French married couple suffering from despondency.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair is the complete loss of hope, the state of hopelessness.

clue.text: Unfriendly landlord, priest recalled

parts.note: a pub landlord is the host

indicators.note: recalled read as called back, so the priest's name runs backwards

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: A surly pub landlord remembered by a priest.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostile describes someone antagonistic, the opposite of friendly.

clue.text: Register seven terraced houses

indicators.note: houses says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Seven terraced houses being put on an official list.
explanation.definitionFit: To register is to enter a name or record in a list or book.

clue.text: Peering, one of five wearing fleece

indicators.note: wearing means the fleece goes on around the quin like a garment

parts.note: to fleece is to swindle, to sting
a quin is one of quintuplets, five babies born together

explanation.surface: A quintuplet in a woolly fleece, peering at something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleece' looks like a garment, but here it is the verb: to cheat someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Squinting is looking with eyes half shut, peering narrowly at something.

clue.text: Sausage dish: one hotel had it prepared

indicators.note: prepared as a cook prepares food, so the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: A hotel served a sausage dish that it had cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: TOAD-IN-THE-HOLE is a British dish of sausages baked in Yorkshire pudding batter.
explanation.definitionFit: This classic British dinner consists of sausages cooked in batter, so it is a sausage dish.

clue.text: Lid of trophy turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a pot is slang for a trophy or cup

explanation.surface: The lid of a trophy cup appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: A top is a cover or cap placed over a container, a lid.

clue.text: Desperately need tot in custody

indicators.note: desperately suggests wild disorder, so these letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A small child is in urgent need of being held in care.
explanation.definitionFit: Detention is the state of being held in custody or confinement.

clue.text: The day before man finally evicted from flat

indicators.note: evicted from means thrown out, so that letter leaves the flat

parts.note: even means flat or level

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word man

explanation.surface: On the eve of the date, a man was finally thrown out of his flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Eve is the evening or day just before an event, as in Christmas Eve.

clue.text: Photograph taken by mate, one in cinema

indicators.note: taken by means the photograph is followed by the mate

parts.note: a photograph is a picture
a pal is a mate, a friend
an ace counts as one in cards

explanation.surface: A friend snapped a photo of someone sitting in the cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture palace is the old-fashioned British term for a large movie theatre.

clue.text: Second pressing

definitions.meaning: a very short moment of time

explanation.definitionFit: An instant is a moment of time, like a second, and instant also means urgent, like pressing.

clue.text: Cleaner forced to go topless in farce

parts.note: a char is a cleaning woman, a charlady

indicators.note: topless means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: made means forced, as in made someone do it

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady forced to strip off in a ridiculous situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Char' is British for a cleaning lady (charwoman).
explanation.definitionFit: A charade is an absurd pretence, a farce.

clue.text: Rubber, strangely rare round south-east

indicators.note: round means the rearranged letters surround the direction
strangely means oddly, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rubber found oddly seldom in the south-east of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a rubber is the thing that removes pencil marks.

clue.text: Measuring device capturing old falling star

indicators.note: capturing means holding, so the device encloses the old letter

parts.note: a meter is a device for measuring, like a gas meter

explanation.surface: An instrument records an elderly star in decline.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooting or falling star is a meteor burning up in the atmosphere.

clue.text: Replaced nurse felt bitter

indicators.note: replaced means put back in a different place, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nurse who was replaced on the ward felt aggrieved.
explanation.definitionFit: Resentful means feeling bitterness at unfair treatment.

clue.text: Constant speed in old kite

parts.note: C is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
rate is speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: A toy kite flying at a constant speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kite' is RAF slang for an aeroplane; an old, rickety one is a crate.
explanation.definitionFit: Crate is slang for a decrepit aircraft or car, and kite is slang for an aeroplane.

clue.text: Scour round for small jazz band

parts.note: to comb an area is to scour it in a search
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Searching everywhere for a little jazz group.
explanation.definitionFit: Combo is an informal word for a small group of jazz musicians.

clue.text: Staying power of a man — it's staggering

indicators.note: staggering means reeling unsteadily, so the letters lurch into a new order

explanation.surface: A man showing endurance, though he is reeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is endurance, the ability to keep going for a long time.

clue.text: Weigh up close friend missing daughter

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the daughter's letter is dropped

parts.note: a compadre is a close friend, a buddy

explanation.surface: Assessing a close friend whose daughter has gone missing.
explanation.definitionFit: To compare things is to weigh them up against each other.

clue.text: What sounds like bent grass?

indicators.note: the question asks for a word heard the same as the one meaning bent

parts.note: wry means bent or twisted, as in a wry neck

explanation.surface: A question about some kind of grass called bent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent grass' looks like a single plant name (bent is indeed a grass), but bent is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye is a cereal plant, a member of the grass family.

clue.text: Assessing some brat in group

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Judging a badly behaved child among a crowd of others.
explanation.definitionFit: Rating something is evaluating or judging its worth.

clue.text: Definitely not name of nobleman left out

indicators.note: out here means left out, so the left letter is omitted from the nobleman

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman

explanation.surface: A nobleman's name was left off a list, emphatically not by accident.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom 'no fear' is an emphatic refusal, meaning certainly not.
